purpose: Authoritative-vendor delta adding Mitti (formerly SafetyCulture), Augury and Evotix as manufacturing-relevant integration targets at spec-verified only. Reuses existing REST/webhook/SCIM/file/vendor-thin profiles, records least-privilege and customer-value boundaries, and adds no tenant, round-trip or write evidence.

systems.name: Mitti (formerly SafetyCulture)
systems.evidenceNote: Mitti's current developer documentation states that SafetyCulture is now Mitti, documents https://api.mitti.com as the long-term API host, and says the legacy https://api.safetyculture.io host still works with no shutoff date announced. The API uses bearer API tokens, supports service-user tokens for long-running integrations, enforces the token owner's permissions/content access, documents incremental modified-since style synchronisation, webhooks, pagination and 429 rate-limit headers, and exposes inspections, users, issues/actions and assets among other areas. WFM pins the approved hostname rather than silently following a rebrand/redirect, uses only read permissions, and treats webhooks as a signal with scheduled catch-up sync. No account token or tenant data was used.

requiredPermissions: prefer a dedicated service-user API token for long-running WFM integration rather than a personal user token
grant only the minimum site/content read access needed for approved inspections, issues/actions, users and assets; avoid Manage all data because it can override narrower access controls
pin api.mitti.com or an explicitly approved documented legacy host and do not silently follow cross-host redirects during the SafetyCulture-to-Mitti transition
verify webhook authenticity and use scheduled incremental reconciliation as a fallback for missed events
dataAvailableOrExpected: inspections/checklists with template, site, completion/modification timestamps and attached media references
issues/incidents with site, category, assignee/collaborator, priority, status and timestamps
actions including due/completion state, assignees, originating inspection or sensor-alert context and site
users with status and system user fields plus customer-defined user metadata where exposed
assets with customer codes, type, site, status and custom fields
near-real-time webhook notifications plus incremental modified-since style polling for reconciliation
automationOpportunities: surface data-minimised safety/risk signals to supervisors when staffing or assigning work while keeping detailed incident narratives outside normal WFM ingestion
correlate inspections, issues and actions with sites/shifts to identify recurring operational-risk and staffing patterns
use asset/site identifiers to reconcile maintenance or inspection activity to work centres without making Mitti the production-system master
reduce duplicate user/site administration by reconciling Mitti identities and sites against HCM/WFM masters
use webhooks for prompt awareness while scheduled modified-since reconciliation repairs missed or delayed event delivery
savingsHypotheses: reduce manual safety-to-workforce reconciliation by linking approved risk signals and actions to the correct site and shift
reduce supervisor administration by reusing existing inspections/issues/actions rather than re-keying safety follow-up into WFM
improve prevention and staffing decisions by identifying repeated inspection or issue patterns before they become disruption or absence
reduce integration fragility during the SafetyCulture-to-Mitti transition by explicitly handling documented host aliases and incremental sync
dataGaps: Mitti is not the authoritative source for employment contracts, payroll, full absence, production demand or broad qualification rules
site/content visibility depends on the service user's effective permissions and sharing rules and must be tenant-proven
custom user fields cannot be used for every server-side filter and customer-defined fields require mapping discovery
sensitive incident or health content must be reduced to the minimum WFM restriction/risk signal rather than copied wholesale
constraintsRisks: Manage all data can override narrower issue/site access and is therefore unsuitable as the default WFM read role
API throttling returns 429 with rate-limit headers and requires backoff/checkpointing
the old SafetyCulture hostname still responds while api.mitti.com is the long-term host, so hostname migration must be explicitly pinned and reviewed
webhooks are not a replacement for reconciliation polling and require authenticity, replay and dedupe controls
the API is also write-capable, so the read connector must not inherit create/update/delete permissions
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST and signed-webhook profiles. In an authorised Mitti tenant, create a dedicated least-privilege service user, pin the approved API hostname, prove read-only access to representative inspections/issues/actions/users/assets, test cursor/page limits plus 429 handling and modified-since checkpoints, validate webhook authenticity/replay/dedupe, and normalise only data-minimised site/risk/action/asset signals before promotion beyond spec verification.

systems.name: Augury Machine Health
systems.evidenceNote: Augury's current vendor material documents public APIs for custom integrations and explicitly states that machine insights can be published to historian/SCADA layers via REST APIs. It also documents closed-loop CMMS/EAM integrations, including SAP PM, IBM Maximo and MaintainX, where machine-health findings can trigger work orders and completed repair information can return to Augury. Public pages do not expose a complete API endpoint/authentication/scope/rate-limit contract, so WFM records only spec verification and keeps all work-order creation, CMMS write-back and Augury agent/action surfaces outside the read connector. No customer environment or credentials were used.

requiredPermissions: dedicated read access to the minimum machine-health/diagnostic/status data exposed through the customer's approved Augury API integration
no CMMS/EAM work-order creation authority in the WFM read connector even where Augury supports closed-loop automation
no Augury agent/autonomous-action authority without a separate action certification and customer approval
tenant/site and asset scopes must be proven from authorised API documentation or sandbox before authentication evidence advances
dataAvailableOrExpected: machine health status and prioritised fault/alarm context
affected machine/component context, diagnostics, severity/urgency and recommended repair guidance where exposed
repair/work-order linkage and post-repair validation context in integrated maintenance workflows
machine/asset and site context used by the customer's Augury deployment
production/process-health insights where licensed and exposed to the customer's API surface
automationOpportunities: adjust maintenance labour and skill demand from actual machine-health severity rather than calendar maintenance alone
identify likely downtime windows early enough to redeploy operators or reduce avoidable overtime
prioritise technician coverage by affected component, severity and recommended action while keeping human approval for work execution
link machine-health outcomes with labour, shift and maintenance records to measure whether staffing/repair decisions reduced downtime
after separately certified write paths, coordinate approved CMMS work-order workflows without granting those rights to the read connector
savingsHypotheses: reduce emergency overtime by scheduling qualified maintenance labour before predicted failures become unplanned downtime
reduce paid idle time by redeploying production labour when high-confidence machine-health evidence indicates a constrained line
improve maintenance productivity by routing the right skill coverage against prioritised diagnostic context instead of broad reactive call-outs
improve labour-to-downtime attribution by combining WFM shift/cost records with machine-health and repair outcomes
dataGaps: public vendor pages do not publish the complete API endpoint, authentication, scope, pagination or rate-limit contract
Augury is not the source of truth for worker identity, contracts, absence, payroll, broad skills or agency labour
available machine/process fields depend on purchased Augury products, deployed assets and customer integration configuration
diagnostic recommendations are operational evidence and must not become automatic machine-control or worker-safety authority
constraintsRisks: public APIs are confirmed but least-privilege read scopes must be tenant/sandbox proven before use
vendor-supported closed-loop maintenance is inherently write-capable and remains separated from WFM's read data plane
machine-health severity may be derived analytics rather than raw sensor truth, so provenance and observation time must be retained
asset identity must reconcile to CMMS/MES/WFM work-centre identifiers before staffing automation can be trusted
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing REST profile only. Obtain authorised Augury API documentation or sandbox credentials, prove the exact read authentication/scope/rate-limit model, enumerate tenant/site/asset identity, retrieve representative machine-health/diagnostic/repair-status records, preserve derived-analytics provenance and timestamps, and normalise machine-state/downtime/maintenance-risk signals before any promotion beyond spec verification. Keep work-order creation and other bidirectional automation behind a separate write evidence path.

systems.name: Evotix EHS & ESG
systems.evidenceNote: Evotix's current integration page documents inbound/outbound APIs, scheduled file-based imports, SCIM for identity lifecycle, middleware/iPaaS patterns and exchange of users/organisational structures, contractor, incident, asset and people data. Evotix has also publicly documented API OAuth support. Because the public integration page does not publish a complete REST/OpenAPI contract, the generic Evotix API is deliberately represented through the vendor-thin adapter rather than guessed as REST; SCIM and file routes reuse their existing protocol profiles. SCIM provisioning and outbound/bidirectional APIs remain write-gated. No tenant or credentials were used.

requiredPermissions: use the minimum read/reporting API or scheduled export access provided for the customer's Evotix product and subscription
SCIM may be used for identity/site reconciliation but provisioning/deprovisioning remains separately write-gated
scheduled files must use customer-approved storage/transfer, integrity checking, idempotency and quarantine before ingestion
do not assume a generic REST contract until authorised product-specific API documentation proves protocol, OAuth/scopes and rate limits
dataAvailableOrExpected: contractor and people data used by the customer's EHS workflows
incident, audit/inspection, risk, action and asset information exposed through approved reporting/API/export routes
identity lifecycle data through SCIM where enabled
environment/sustainability metrics and operational-risk context where licensed and exposed
automationOpportunities: reconcile contractor/worker/site identity into WFM to reduce duplicate administration while keeping HCM/VMS authoritative
surface data-minimised incident/risk/restriction signals to workforce scheduling and compliance workflows
correlate recurring audit/inspection/risk patterns with shift, overtime and staffing outcomes
use approved file/API exports to accelerate implementation where direct product APIs are not available to the customer
after separate write certification, automate approved identity lifecycle or EHS follow-up workflows without granting those permissions to the read connector
savingsHypotheses: reduce duplicate worker/contractor/site maintenance by reconciling existing Evotix organisational data with WFM masters
reduce manual safety reporting and supervisor follow-up by reusing approved incident/risk/action data
reduce implementation effort by supporting the vendor's documented SCIM, file and middleware/iPaaS integration patterns rather than demanding a bespoke connector
improve staffing/compliance decisions by using data-minimised risk and restriction evidence instead of separate spreadsheets
dataGaps: product-specific API endpoint schemas, OAuth/scopes, pagination and rate limits are not fully public on the current integration page
Evotix product editions have distinct architectures and availability varies by product/subscription
employment contract, payroll, broad absence and production truth usually remain outside Evotix
incident and occupational-health records may contain highly sensitive information and normally require derived/minimised WFM signals
constraintsRisks: inbound/outbound APIs and SCIM are write-capable; WFM keeps provisioning and follow-up mutations disabled by default
scheduled files can be partial, duplicated or stale and require checksum, schema, watermark and quarantine controls
product/edition differences mean interface availability must be proven per tenant rather than inferred from marketing material
EHS/occupational-health content requires strict minimisation, retention and role segregation
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Reuse the existing SCIM, file-batch and vendor-thin profiles without inventing a REST contract. Obtain authorised Evotix product-specific API documentation or sandbox access, identify the customer's available inbound/outbound/reporting surface and OAuth/scope model, prove read-only user/org/contractor/incident/asset exports, validate SCIM read reconciliation plus file integrity/schema/idempotency controls, and normalise only data-minimised safety/contractor/site signals before promotion beyond spec verification.
